key_insight: AdaSR enables large reasoning models to think and adapt while data is still arriving, instead of waiting for a full input first. It improves streaming reasoning by learning how to update decisions online with a hierarchical policy optimization strategy.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the mismatch between static, read-then-think reasoning models and real-world streaming settings like audio and video, where information arrives incrementally and the model must reason under partial observations.
method: Introduces adaptive streaming reasoning so the model can read, think, and revise decisions continuously as new tokens/frames arrive.
Uses hierarchical relative policy optimization to better train streaming behavior beyond simple supervised imitation of fixed reasoning traces.
Targets dynamic inputs and partial-information settings, aiming for more robust online updates and response generation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, AdaSR offers a path toward more practical reasoning systems that can operate in real-time, event-driven environments. This is especially useful for applications like live audio/video understanding, monitoring, and interactive assistants.
visual_elements: A side-by-side pipeline showing read-then-think vs. adaptive streaming reasoning
A timeline/stream diagram of incoming tokens or frames with iterative reasoning updates
A hierarchical policy tree illustrating relative policy optimization
An application icon set for audio, video, and live monitoring use cases
paper_title: AdaSR: Adaptive Streaming Reasoning with Hierarchical Relative Policy Optimization
paper_authors: Junlong Tong, Wenqi Xu, Yingqi Fan, Anhao Zhao, Xuan Lu
